# s210 — Record which item discovered new work

Discovered work needs a validated source-item reference rather than prose embedded in findings.

**Findings:** agents feedback 2026-10-05 U4a; docs/feedback/agents-2026-10-05.md · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-05** — Ready for review: Added optional fields.discovered_from with index schema 5, existing-source validation before allocation, outline parsing and whole-batch validation, exact-source list filtering, Markdown/HTML annotations and custom row placeholder, purge reference guards and dangling-source integrity checks. Retirement preserves sources; provenance does not affect pickup or scores. Updated command/import/agent/configuration documentation, architecture, and changelog. All 10 focused provenance tests pass. Full unittest discovery: 1250 tests, OK (1 skipped), using worktree-local TMPDIR. Affected-test selection required full discovery because its map was missing. Tracking check and git diff --check pass.

**Not in this slice:** duplicate detection, filing keys, changing status defaults, or turning provenance into a dependency or priority edge.

## Why

U4's orchestrator files discovered defects as drafts and wants to trace them to the finding slice. add and outline currently expose no provenance field. Status remains the caller's configured choice.

## Files

Item model, add/import operations, outline parser and reporting, CLI add/list, roadmap rendering, integrity checks, associated tests and command/import/agent documentation.

## Failing tests

- Add and outline input accept an existing source ID, including done or retired sources, preserve it in JSON, and show it on the generated row.
- Unknown sources fail before allocation, logging or rendering; a mixed invalid outline writes nothing.
- List filtering uses exact source ID and composes with existing status/tree filters. Unknown filter IDs fail with no_such_item; zero matches succeed.
- Missing historical fields load empty without writes, lean omits them, and empty provenance leaves row rendering unchanged.
- A source reference does not block pickup or alter scores. Purge refuses deletion of a referenced source unless explicitly forced; forced dangling provenance is reported by integrity validation.

## Implement

Store discovered_from as an optional string in Item.fields. Add discovered-from to add/list and the single-value discovered_from outline key. Require an existing ID in the current project before allocation; the outline may refer to existing IDs, not prospective title-based source references. A source can have any status.

Render a source annotation only when present, supplying it to default row rendering and documenting custom-template support. Keep this independent of depends_on. Extend integrity and purge-reference checks so ordinary removal/retirement preserves references and purging cannot silently orphan them.

Bump the index schema for saved provenance; older files retain an empty default, and older readers refuse newer state rather than dropping the reference. Update outline known-key diagnostics, command contracts, and changelog.

## Check

Run add/import/list/provenance/purge validation cases, then full unittest discovery, tracking check, and git diff --check. Inspect a generated row with source provenance and an unchanged row without it.

Use the project's ignored TMPDIR for temporary test fixtures, and scoped
support.isolated_discovery only for fixtures that require outside-project
discovery. The repository acceptance commands, run against the implementation
checkout's code and state, are:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check --json
git diff --check
```
